I'm probably mentioning things that will make everything more complicated if you only have a small operation. The type of inbound email sparkpost offers is actually more advanced than simply forwarding the email to your mailbox. However, when you buy a domain from some place like this: https://www.namesilo.com/Support/Email-Forwarding, they will have a feature called email forwarding. That will keep things simple. When you send out email though, you should really use sparkpost to track things like deliverability. You will also want them to help you do email campaigns. For responding to customer inquries, you can start with an SMTP relay at sparkpost. This means that the mailbox you chose should support sending email over SMTP (externally). When you get more customers, you will want a service like this: http://alternativeto.net/software/zendesk/ . With it, reading and responding to customer inquiries will be done through the helpdesk. Obviously, things get more complicated when your employees need their own mailbox. You will need to move away from email forwarding and actually have an email service provider.
